title: The fire
hookLine: described so people turn back in time
last: AT THE PROPHET'S POOL, THIRST ENDS FOR GOOD.

cards: A sign on a mountain road: sharp bend ahead, slow down. Nobody puts it there to frighten drivers for fun. It's there because someone wants them to make the turn.
The Qur'an speaks of the fire in plain, hard language, and first-time readers sometimes stop there.
But the Qur'an itself says why the warning is given, and the hadith add a surprising detail about how small the way out can be.

teach.b: In Arabic the fire is simply an-nar, and the Qur'an gives it other names too. Muslims hold it as real, part of the unseen they believe in, alongside the pool and the garden. The descriptions are not soft.
But look at the frame. In one passage, after describing the fire, the Qur'an says this is how Allah warns His servants, then turns straight to them: so be mindful of Me.

teach.h: A WARNING, SPOKEN TO THE LIVING.
teach.b: The picture comes with an address, spoken to people who still have time. The Qur'an also draws a line.

teach.h: TURN BACK BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE.
teach.b: Forgiveness is for those who do wrong in ignorance and turn back soon, not for one who keeps doing evil until death arrives and only then says, now I repent. So the warning is about timing: turn back in time.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet, peace be upon him, tells people to protect themselves from the fire, even with half a date given in charity. Not a fortune, not a lifetime of perfection.
Half a piece of fruit, given to someone hungry. Another report adds: if you don't have even that, then with a kind word.

The same tradition that describes the fire in hard language makes the door out very small and very near. Muslim scholars have discussed the fire's nature in detail, and they don't all agree on every question.
But on the purpose of the warning, the text is clear. It's a sign before the bend.

how: Muslims affirm the fire as part of belief in the Last Day; some teachers present its descriptions alongside the hadith about protecting oneself even with half a date in charity, and Muslims ask Allah's forgiveness for wrongs they turn away from.

o: the heat of the desert sun that pilgrims endure at midday
the sacred flame kept burning in a mosque's prayer niche
the fire of the hereafter, described as a warning to the living

p: spoken to people who still have time
given in charity, a shield from the fire

s: in the Qur'an, the descriptions of the fire come with a call to turn back
after one description, the text turns to the listeners: so be mindful of Me.
the Qur'an says turning back counts the same at any moment, even as death arrives
it says forgiveness is not for one who keeps doing evil until death and only then repents.
the hadith says only a great fortune in charity protects from the fire
the Prophet said even half a date, and if not that, a kind word.

games.q: you want to protect yourself from the fire, but you have almost nothing to give. what does the hadith say?
o: wait until you can give a lot.
games.why: in Bukhari the Prophet says to protect yourselves from the fire even with half a date in charity, and if not that, with a kind word.

practice: Let one small wrong come to mind, something you've been doing lately and would rather stop: a sharp word, a habit, a corner you keep cutting.

Without judging yourself, picture the bend in the road, and picture taking the turn: one concrete thing you'll do differently. If you pray, ask Allah's forgiveness in your own words; if not, simply hold the decision.

wordCard.voice: The fire. An-nar: described in the Qur'an in hard language, as a warning spoken to people who still have time to turn back. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: turn back in time. Even half a date can be the turn. Tomorrow, the garden.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1417 and 6023 (protect yourselves from the fire even with half a date; if not, a kind word)
